## L17 — "Document every command and finding"

- **Lexical marker:** none (positive imperative, no §5b marker)
- **Skip class:** `skip-no-trigger`
- **Skip reason:** No observable signal. What counts as "documented"? Tool
  calls don't have an `is_documented` field; there's no way for the harness
  to detect a missing log entry. The agent following the skill body will
  document; the harness can't verify it. The LLM policy gate could
  *probabilistically* judge whether the agent's report includes per-command
  notes, but the FP rate would be high (e.g., succinct true-positive cases).
- **Could be enforced if:** The source rewrote this as a concrete obligation —
  e.g., "After every Bash command, write a one-line entry to `./forensics.log`."
  Then a PostToolUse advisory could check whether recent file_writes include
  that path. See §15.4 of the `/enforce` skill for the trigger-extraction
  pattern.

## L143 — "Work only on provided images and files"

- **Lexical marker:** "Only"
- **Skip class:** `skip-abstract-trigger`
- **Skip reason:** "Provided" is context state the harness can't observe.
  The agent could be working on any image with no way for us to know which
  were originally supplied. The LLM policy gate could judge this with
  trajectory + authorization context, but the policy is downstream of and
  weaker than P1 (which already blocks writes to evidence-pattern paths
  unconditionally).
- **Could be enforced if:** The source declared an explicit allowlist —
  e.g., "Only operate on images listed in `./engagement-images.txt`." A
  path-vs-allowlist check is then deterministic.

## L145 — "Document chain of custody for real investigations"

- **Lexical marker:** none

- **Skip reason:** Documentation directive without a tool-call shape. Same

  discriminator the harness can't detect — CTF vs. real engagement is user
